title: Neo4j Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Neo4j course.

entries.name: Create a node with a label
entries.summary: A node represents one thing. A label says what kind of thing it is, and properties hold its named facts.

entries.name: Find a node by a property
entries.summary: MATCH finds graph patterns. A property condition can choose the node with a known id.

entries.name: Add a uniqueness rule
entries.summary: A uniqueness constraint prevents two nodes with a label from sharing the same chosen property value.

example.code: CREATE CONSTRAINT cma_book_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (b:Book) REQUIRE b.id IS UNIQUE;

entries.name: Match or create with MERGE
entries.summary: MERGE finds a pattern or creates it if missing.

example.code: MERGE (b:Book {id:'cma-b2'}) SET b.title='Garden Days',b.pages=40 RETURN b.title;

entries.name: Connect a reader to a book
entries.summary: A relationship gives two nodes a named connection and direction.

example.code:
MERGE (r:Reader {id:'cma-r1'}) SET r.name='Mia'
WITH r MATCH (b:Book {id:'cma-b1'}) MERGE (r)-[:READ]->(b) RETURN r.name,b.title;

entries.name: Follow a relationship
entries.summary: A pattern can follow a known relationship to related nodes.

entries.name: Filter nodes with WHERE
entries.summary: WHERE adds a condition to a matched pattern.

example.code: MATCH (b:Book) WHERE b.id STARTS WITH "cma-" AND b.pages>=50 RETURN b.title,b.pages;

entries.name: Sort and limit graph results
entries.summary: ORDER BY sorts returned rows from a graph query.

example.code: MATCH (b:Book) WHERE b.id STARTS WITH 'cma-' RETURN b.title,b.pages ORDER BY b.pages,b.title LIMIT 1;

entries.name: Count connected books
entries.summary: An aggregate can summarise matched relationships.

entries.name: Keep a reader with no match
entries.summary: OPTIONAL MATCH keeps the earlier row even when the optional connection is missing.

example.code:
MERGE (r:Reader {id:'cma-r2'}) SET r.name='Sam'
WITH r OPTIONAL MATCH (r)-[:READ]->(b:Book) RETURN r.name,b.title;

entries.name: Change a relationship fact
entries.summary: Relationships can hold properties too. A property can describe the connection itself, such as when a reader finished a book.

entries.name: Remove one practice node carefully
entries.summary: A connected node cannot be deleted normally while its relationships remain.
